classes.objetivo: Reconocer cuándo una respuesta amable en inglés equivale a un rechazo o a un desacuerdo y entender su significado real.

ensenanza.en: An indirect refusal such as “I am afraid that might be difficult” spares the listener's feelings, but it rarely opens a negotiation.
ensenanza.es: Un rechazo indirecto como «Me temo que eso podría ser difícil» ahorra disgustos al oyente, pero rara vez abre una negociación.
ensenanza.nota: Suavizador + vaguedad sin alternativa suele significar «no».

ensenanza.en: “We must have lunch sometime” is a polite brush-off, not an invitation, unless a day and a place follow.
ensenanza.es: «Tenemos que comer juntos algún día» es un rechazo cortés y vago, no una invitación, a menos que sigan un día y un lugar.
ensenanza.nota: Sin día ni hora no hay plan real.

ensenanza.en: A tactful manager who says “I will think about it” without a date may simply turn down your idea.
ensenanza.es: Un jefe con tacto que dice «Lo pensaré» sin dar fecha puede estar rechazando simplemente tu idea.
ensenanza.nota: «I will think about it» sin plazo suele ser un no cortés.

ensenanza.en: To be honest, “with respect” rarely introduces praise; it usually warns you that a disagreement is coming.
ensenanza.es: Siendo sincero, «con todo respeto» rara vez introduce un elogio; suele avisar de que llega un desacuerdo.
ensenanza.nota: With respect anuncia un desacuerdo, no admiración.

ensenanza.en: Learners who take the hint hear the doubt behind a polite refusal and stop asking instead of waiting for a clearer answer.
ensenanza.es: Quienes captan la indirecta oyen la duda tras un rechazo cortés y dejan de insistir en vez de esperar una respuesta más clara.
ensenanza.nota: Take the hint: entender lo que se insinúa sin que se diga.

ensenanza.en: A tactful person who wants to leave the door open will always add an alternative, such as “perhaps next month”.
ensenanza.es: Una persona con tacto que quiere dejar la puerta abierta siempre añade una alternativa, como «quizá el mes que viene».
ensenanza.nota: La alternativa concreta es lo que distingue un «quizá» real de un «no» amable.

explicacion.texto: En muchos contextos del inglés, sobre todo el británico y el profesional, se evita el «no» directo. Se usan frases amables que funcionan como rechazo o desacuerdo: «That might be difficult», «I will think about it», «We must have lunch sometime», «With respect…». Las pistas: modales de duda (might, could), minimizadores (a bit, slightly) y la ausencia de fecha o alternativa. No es falsedad, es cortesía; en español un «no puedo» directo suele ser más aceptable. Es una tendencia: el contexto manda.

patron.texto: Suavizador + frase vaga + sin compromiso = rechazo cortés:

formula.nota: modal de duda: might en lugar de «no puedo»
sin fecha ni alternativa: no hay compromiso

filas.texto: With respect, I see it differently.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am not agree with you, with respect.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: With respect, I do not agree with you.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En inglés se dice I do not agree (verbo agree con do), no «I am not agree»; y With respect suele ir al principio.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I will think it and tell you.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I will think about it and tell you.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Think necesita about: think about it significa «pensarlo».

situacion.contexto: Mia le cuenta a Leo que Tom no respondió como ella esperaba.

dialogo.texto: Tom said “That might be difficult” when I asked him to help on Saturday.
dialogo.traduccion: Tom dijo «Eso podría ser difícil» cuando le pedí ayuda el sábado.

dialogo.texto: In English that is usually a polite no. Did he offer another day?
dialogo.traduccion: En inglés eso suele ser un no cortés. ¿Ofreció otro día?

dialogo.texto: No. He only said he was busy.
dialogo.traduccion: No. Solo dijo que estaba ocupado.

dialogo.texto: Then it is a no. Say thanks and ask somebody else.
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces es un no. Da las gracias y pídeselo a otra persona.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué concluye Leo sobre «That might be difficult»?

opciones.es: Que Tom probablemente rechaza la petición.
Que Tom ayudará si se lo piden otra vez.
Que Tom necesita más tiempo para decidir.

item.feedback: Leo explica que en inglés suele ser un no cortés, y Tom no ofreció otro día: es un rechazo indirecto.

guiada.consigna: Lee la escena: ¿qué suele significar la respuesta de la vecina?
guiada.texto: Leo asked his neighbour to lend him a ladder on Saturday. She smiled and said, “I am afraid it is a little awkward this weekend, but I will see what I can do.” She did not mention another day.
opciones: It is probably a polite no, since she offers no other day.
She will certainly bring the ladder on Saturday morning, before lunch.
She will lend it if Leo asks again on Sunday.
guiada.feedback: Un «I am afraid» con un obstáculo vago y sin día alternativo es la estructura típica de un rechazo cortés.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en que no propone ninguna alternativa concreta.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «No quería rechazar la oferta con brusquedad.»
guiada.texto: The company could not afford the project, but it did not want to ___ the offer rudely, so the director wrote a warm and rather vague reply.
guiada.feedback: Turn down es el verbo frasal habitual para rechazar una oferta o una invitación.

guiada.consigna: Relaciona cada frase indirecta con lo que suele significar.
pares: I am afraid that might be difficult
With respect, I see it differently
guiada.feedback: Las tres primeras se leen como rechazos o desacuerdos; la última deja abierta una posibilidad real.
guiada.pista: Busca en cada frase si hay una fecha o una alternativa.

practica.consigna: Escucha la anécdota: ¿qué hace que su respuesta equivalga a un rechazo?
practica.audio: When I invited my colleague to the company picnic, he said that it sounded lovely and that he would like to come in principle, but that the weekend was a little difficult for him. I waited for him to suggest another date, but he only smiled and asked about the weather. Later I realised that he had turned me down, as politely as possible.
opciones: He praised the plan but offered no other date.
He said that another appointment made the weekend impossible.
He accepted and then cancelled on the same morning.
He asked the writer to send the invitation again in writing.
practica.feedback: Elogia el plan, pero no propone otra fecha ni se compromete: esa ausencia de alternativa es la pista de un rechazo cortés.

practica.consigna: Lee el correo: ¿qué hace realmente quien escribe con su mensaje?
practica.texto: With respect, I am not sure that moving the deadline is the best option. I appreciate the client's pressure, but I wonder whether the team has enough time to do the work well. Perhaps we could discuss it on Monday.
opciones: The writer disagrees politely with the proposal.
The writer accepts the proposal with some doubts.
The writer asks the client for a new deadline.
The writer changes her mind because of the client's pressure.
practica.feedback: «With respect» anuncia el desacuerdo y «I wonder whether» lo suaviza; proponer hablar el lunes es cortesía, no aceptación.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Un rechazo con tacto deja la puerta abierta a otro día.»
practica.respuesta: A tactful refusal leaves the door open for another day
practica.feedback: El sujeto es a tactful refusal; leaves the door open expresa que se ofrece una alternativa.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el relato: ¿qué aprende quien narra sobre los elogios en inglés?
evaluacion.audio: When I first moved to London, I kept a list of phrases that confused me. My manager's “I will think about it” meant no. A neighbour's “we must have a drink sometime” was just goodbye. The worst was a colleague who called mine a very “brave” idea. I thanked him warmly, went home happy and spent the weekend developing it. On Monday my manager quietly removed it from the agenda. Only then did a friend explain that brave, in that tone, means “probably a mistake”. Since then I listen to what people do not say as carefully as to what they do.
opciones: That polite praise can hide doubt, so tone and context matter.
That managers in London reject ideas without ever saying why.
That people in London rarely mean what they say to strangers.
That a neighbour's vague invitation is best taken at face value.
evaluacion.feedback: «Brave» sonaba a elogio, pero en ese tono significaba «probablemente un error»: aprendió a escuchar lo que no se dice, sin concluir que nadie habla en serio.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué quiere decir en realidad quien escribe este correo?
evaluacion.texto: Dear Jordan, thank you for the proposal. I can see that a great deal of work went into it, and I am sure it will find a good home somewhere. At the moment, however, our priorities lie elsewhere, and I would not want you to spend more time on it on our account. I hope that we can keep in touch.
opciones: The proposal is rejected, and the writer hopes to end the matter kindly.
The proposal may be accepted when the company's priorities change.
The writer wants Jordan to rewrite it for another department next year.
The writer is asking him to wait a few more weeks.
evaluacion.feedback: «Somewhere» y «elsewhere» lo sitúan fuera de su empresa, y pedirle que no invierta más tiempo es el rechazo definitivo con cortesía.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Si no te dan fecha, capta la indirecta y busca otra salida.»
evaluacion.texto: If you have asked twice and still have no date, it is time to take the ___ and find another way forward.
evaluacion.feedback: Take the hint es la expresión fija para captar lo que se insinúa sin que se diga.

evaluacion.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con su significado real según la situación.
pares: “That is an interesting idea,” said after a two-minute pitch
“I will think about it and call you on Thursday,” said while writing in a diary
es una respuesta provisional con plazo real
“With respect…” at the start of a reply
“I cannot on Friday; could we try Monday?”
evaluacion.feedback: La misma fórmula cambia según el contexto: una fecha o una alternativa concreta convierte el rechazo en una posibilidad real.

repaso.consigna: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe ante la indirección en inglés?
repaso.texto: In my country, a direct “no” is a sign of honesty. In England I learnt to hear something else in “perhaps”. It took me a year to see that nobody was being dishonest; they were protecting the relationship, not hiding the truth. I still prefer a clear answer, but I no longer think that a soft one is a lie.
opciones: The writer now reads the soft style as courtesy, though clarity is still preferred.
The writer finds the soft style dishonest and avoids English speakers whenever possible.
The writer has copied the indirect style and dislikes clear answers.
The writer thinks that every soft answer hides a secret refusal.
repaso.feedback: Ya no cree que una respuesta suave sea una mentira, pero sigue prefiriendo la claridad: comprensión sin adoptar el estilo.

repaso.respuesta: They were not lying; they were being tactful
repaso.feedback: Were being + adjetivo describe una actitud del momento: tactful explica por qué la respuesta era suave.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el mensaje: ¿es probable que la hablante asista a la fiesta?
repaso.audio: Hi Sara, thanks for the invitation to your party. It sounds wonderful, and I would love to be there if I can. The week is a bit crowded at the moment, so I cannot promise anything. I will let you know if things change.
opciones: Probably not: she promises nothing and suggests no alternative.
Yes: she will arrive late, but she will certainly come.
Yes: she only needs Sara to send the invitation again.
Probably: she will confirm as soon as she finishes work.
repaso.feedback: Elogia el plan pero no se compromete, no da fecha y no propone otra ocasión: es un rechazo cortés, no un sí aplazado.

classes.objetivo: Sustituir afirmaciones absolutas por generalizaciones matizadas con tend to, by and large, as a rule e it is not unusual for.

ensenanza.en: An absolute statement such as “All teenagers are lazy” collapses as soon as you meet one exception, so careful speakers avoid it.
ensenanza.es: Una afirmación absoluta como «Todos los adolescentes son perezosos» se derrumba en cuanto conoces una excepción, así que los hablantes cuidadosos la evitan.
ensenanza.nota: Todos, siempre y nunca son absolutos: casi nunca son justos.

ensenanza.en: Typical travellers return with a sweeping generalisation about a whole nation and forget everyone they did not meet.
ensenanza.es: Los viajeros típicos vuelven con una generalización demasiado amplia sobre toda una nación y olvidan a todos los que no conocieron.
ensenanza.nota: Una generalización amplia habla de la prisa del viajero, no de la gente.

ensenanza.en: People in my town tend to be punctual and, with few exceptions, they apologise when they are late.
ensenanza.es: En mi ciudad la gente suele ser puntual y, con pocas excepciones, se disculpa cuando llega tarde.
ensenanza.nota: Tend to + verbo base expresa tendencia; with few exceptions la reconoce.

ensenanza.en: By and large, my neighbours are reserved at first but, more often than not, they turn out to be warm and generous.
ensenanza.es: En general, mis vecinos son reservados al principio pero, la mayoría de las veces, resultan ser cálidos y generosos.
ensenanza.nota: By and large abre la frase; more often than not matiza con frecuencia, no con certeza.

ensenanza.en: It is not unusual for a typical family here to eat lunch at two; as a rule, the shops close early.
ensenanza.es: No es raro que una familia típica de aquí coma a las dos; por norma general, las tiendas cierran pronto.
ensenanza.nota: It is not unusual for + sujeto + to + verbo: «no es raro que».

ensenanza.en: To qualify a claim without weakening it, replace absolute words such as all and never with tend to, most or usually.
ensenanza.es: Para matizar una afirmación sin debilitarla, sustituye palabras absolutas como all y never por tend to, most o usually.
ensenanza.nota: Matizar no es dudar: es ajustar lo que dices a lo que puedes sostener.

explicacion.texto: Las afirmaciones absolutas («All people here are rude») casi nunca son ciertas y pueden ofender. Para generalizar con cuidado el inglés ofrece: tend to + verbo base («People tend to be punctual»); marcadores de «en general» al inicio (by and large, as a rule, on the whole); it is not unusual for + sujeto + to + verbo; y cuantificadores como many, most o some en lugar de all. Diferencia con el español: para «soler» el inglés no tiene un verbo idéntico; se usa tend to o usually (y used to, solo para hábitos del pasado), y tend to va seguido de un verbo base.

patron.texto: Marcador + grupo + tend to + verbo base:

formula.nota: verbo base detrás de tend to

filas.texto: People here tend to be punctual.
Shops are always closed on Sundays.
As a rule, shops are closed on Sundays.
It is not unusual for people to eat late.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: People here tends to be punctual.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: People here tend to be punctual.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: People es plural: tend va sin -s.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: People here use to arrive late.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: People here tend to arrive late.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: «Soler» no se dice use to; use to se refiere a hábitos del pasado. Para tendencias actuales, tend to.

situacion.contexto: Leo vuelve de un viaje y habla de la gente de un pueblo.

dialogo.texto: In that town, all the people are rude.
dialogo.traduccion: En ese pueblo, toda la gente es maleducada.

dialogo.texto: All of them? That is an absolute claim.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Toda? Es una afirmación absoluta.

dialogo.texto: Well, most of the people I met were reserved.
dialogo.traduccion: Bueno, la mayoría de las personas que conocí eran reservadas.

dialogo.texto: Better. Say: people there tend to be reserved at first.
dialogo.traduccion: Mejor. Di: allí la gente suele ser reservada al principio.

item.consigna: ¿Qué hace Ana con la frase de Leo?

opciones.es: Le pide una frase más matizada que «all».
Le pide que confirme que todos son maleducados.
Le dice que «reserved» es una palabra prohibida.

item.feedback: Ana señala que «all the people» es absoluto y propone una versión con tend to, más justa y matizada.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué versión corrige mejor la frase absoluta de la estudiante?
guiada.texto: A student wrote in her travel blog: “Everybody in that city is always late, and nobody ever apologises.” Her teacher underlined the absolute words and asked for a more careful version.
opciones: People there tend to be late, and many do not apologise.
Nobody in that city is ever on time, and all of them are rude.
Some people there are sometimes late, but they always apologise.
guiada.feedback: Tend to y many sustituyen a everybody, always y nobody: la versión conserva la observación sin convertirla en ley.
guiada.pista: Busca la versión sin todos, siempre ni nadie.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Por norma general, las tiendas cierran pronto los domingos.»
guiada.texto: Shops here are not all the same, but as a ___, they close early on Sundays, and a few stay open for tourists.
guiada.feedback: As a rule es la fórmula fija para «por norma general» y admite excepciones, como las tiendas para turistas.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «No es raro que la gente coma tarde.»
guiada.respuesta: It is not unusual for people to eat late
guiada.feedback: It is not unusual for + sujeto + to + verbo base: «no es raro que» con sujeto propio.
guiada.pista: Empieza con it is not unusual for.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué defecto tiene la afirmación del hermano?
practica.audio: After a week in the north, my brother came back saying that all the locals were cold. I asked him how many he had actually spoken to. Four, he admitted: a taxi driver, two waiters and a man in a queue. I told him that four people do not make a nation, and that he could safely say only that the people he met had been rather reserved.
opciones: It generalises from a tiny sample to everybody.
It describes the north with too many exceptions.
It depends on one conversation with a taxi driver.
It ignores that waiters are often reserved.
practica.feedback: Cuatro personas no representan a todo un lugar: el error está en pasar de una muestra mínima a un «all» absoluto.

practica.consigna: Lee el párrafo: ¿qué postura mantiene quien escribe?
practica.texto: Teachers often say that teenagers tend to sleep late, and this is mostly true. But it is not true of all teenagers, and I know several who are awake at six. The safest statement is that many teenagers prefer later hours, and that the habit varies from one family to another.
opciones: A general pattern is acceptable if it admits exceptions.
Every statement about teenagers is unfair and should be avoided.
Teenagers sleep late because they are lazy and tired.
The habit of sleeping late is the same in every family.
practica.feedback: Acepta el patrón («tend to»), pero rechaza que valga para todos: la versión segura dice «many» y reconoce la variación.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Con pocas excepciones, aquí la gente suele ser puntual.»
practica.respuesta: With few exceptions, people here tend to be punctual
aceptadas: People here tend to be punctual, with few exceptions
practica.feedback: With few exceptions puede abrir o cerrar la frase; tend to va seguido de un verbo base (be).

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha: ¿cuál es la postura de la investigadora sobre las generalizaciones?
evaluacion.audio: A researcher interviewed on a podcast recently described what she calls the airport effect. A traveller spends two hours in a foreign airport, meets three tired officials and decides that the whole country is unfriendly. The mistake, she says, is not in noticing a pattern, but in announcing it as a law. By and large, she added, people tend to be helpful when they are not exhausted. If you must generalise, leave room for the exceptions, because the exceptions are usually the people who change your mind. Her listeners laughed, but many wrote in afterwards to say that they had been guilty of the airport effect themselves.
opciones: It is fair to notice a pattern, but wrong to present it as a rule with no exceptions.
Travellers should avoid forming any impression of a country from one visit.
Tiredness explains why some people are unfriendly, so the pattern is fair.
Exceptions should be ignored, because they rarely change anybody's mind.
evaluacion.feedback: No condena observar patrones, sino convertirlos en ley: propone generalizar dejando espacio a las excepciones.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué objeta en realidad quien escribe la carta a la reseña?
evaluacion.texto: Your review of our town claims that the locals never smile and that every restaurant closes at nine. I have lived here for forty years. Many people are shy with strangers, and a few restaurants do close early, but the words never and every spoil an otherwise fair piece. A reviewer who wrote most would have been accurate, and I would not be writing this letter.
opciones: The use of absolute words where a hedge would be accurate.
The mention that some residents are shy with strangers.
The fact that the reviewer was a stranger to the town.
The claim that a few restaurants close early.
evaluacion.feedback: Admite que hay gente tímida y restaurantes que cierran pronto: lo que rechaza son never y every, donde most habría sido exacto.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Con pocas excepciones, los vecinos llegan a tiempo.»
evaluacion.texto: Nobody can say that every neighbour is punctual, but with few ___, the people on my street arrive on time and apologise when they are late.
evaluacion.feedback: With few exceptions es la colocación que matiza una generalización sin abandonarla.

evaluacion.consigna: Matiza la frase con una estructura de tendencia (tend to, by and large…).
evaluacion.texto: All English people are cold and nobody talks to strangers.
evaluacion.respuesta: English people tend to be reserved with strangers
aceptadas: By and large, English people are reserved with strangers
As a rule, English people are reserved with strangers
The English tend to be reserved with strangers
English people tend to be cold with strangers
English people tend to be reserved and rarely talk to strangers
By and large, the English are cold with strangers
Most English people tend to be reserved with strangers
evaluacion.feedback: Sustituir all y nobody por tend to o by and large convierte un absoluto en una tendencia que se puede defender.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito menciona a su abuelo quien escribe?
repaso.texto: When people say that all young people are impatient, I think of my grandfather, who demanded his dinner at six sharp every evening. Being impatient is not a problem of one age; it is a human habit, and it tends to appear in every age group. I would gladly replace all with many, and then we could start an honest conversation.
opciones: To show that the trait is not limited to young people.
To prove that her grandfather was more impatient than her friends.
To argue that dinner should always be served at six.
To admit that all young people are impatient after all.
repaso.feedback: El abuelo es un contraejemplo: si la impaciencia aparece en otra edad, no puede atribuirse a todos los jóvenes, y propone cambiar all por many.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Las tiendas de aquí suelen cerrar pronto los domingos.»
repaso.respuesta: Shops here tend to close early on Sundays
repaso.feedback: Shops here es plural, así que tend va sin -s y el verbo que sigue queda en base: close.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué le recomienda Leo a Mia?
repaso.audio: Hi Mia, I read your draft. You wrote that all the locals are rude, and I think that is too strong. Why not say that most of the people you met were reserved? Then nobody can argue with you, and your article will sound more honest.
opciones: To qualify the claim so that it matches what she actually saw.
To replace her examples with the opinions of a few local people.
To keep the claim but add a few examples of rude behaviour.
To drop the topic because it may offend the people she met.
repaso.feedback: Leo no pide callar la observación, sino ajustarla a lo que Mia puede sostener: «most» y «reserved» en lugar de «all» y «rude».

classes.objetivo: Identificar la causa, el supuesto cultural y la mejor reacción en relatos de malentendidos entre culturas.

vocabulario.en: give the benefit of the doubt
vocabulario.es: conceder el beneficio de la duda

ensenanza.en: Many visitors assume that dinner is at nine, a hidden assumption that surprises a host family eating at six.
ensenanza.es: Muchos visitantes suponen que la cena es a las nueve, un supuesto oculto que sorprende a una familia anfitriona que cena a las seis.
ensenanza.nota: Assume = suponer: creemos algo sin haberlo preguntado.

ensenanza.en: Tom felt embarrassed because nobody had told him about the custom of bringing a small gift.
ensenanza.es: Tom se sintió avergonzado porque nadie le había hablado de la costumbre de llevar un pequeño regalo.
ensenanza.nota: Embarrassed describe cómo se siente la persona; embarrassing describe la situación.

ensenanza.en: The misunderstanding began when Mia took “We will see” as a yes, while her host meant it as a polite no.
ensenanza.es: El malentendido empezó cuando Mia tomó «Ya veremos» como un sí, mientras que su anfitrión lo decía como un no cortés.
ensenanza.nota: El supuesto de Mia no coincidía con el del anfitrión.

ensenanza.en: In some families silence is not rude; a guest who stays quiet may come across as thoughtful rather than unfriendly.
ensenanza.es: En algunas familias el silencio no es de mala educación; un invitado que calla puede parecer reflexivo y no antipático.
ensenanza.nota: Lo que parece maleducado en una cultura puede ser cortesía en otra.

ensenanza.en: The exchange student did not take offence; her first reaction was to ask a polite question instead of judging her hosts.
ensenanza.es: La estudiante de intercambio no se ofendió; su primera reacción fue hacer una pregunta educada en lugar de juzgar a sus anfitriones.
ensenanza.nota: La mejor reacción suele ser preguntar con tacto, no acusar.

ensenanza.en: When a custom seems strange, give the benefit of the doubt before you decide that anybody was rude.
ensenanza.es: Cuando una costumbre parece extraña, concede el beneficio de la duda antes de decidir que alguien fue maleducado.
ensenanza.nota: Empieza por suponer buena intención y luego pregunta.

explicacion.texto: Un malentendido cultural casi nunca es mala educación: cada persona parte de un supuesto (assumption) distinto sobre la hora de cenar, los zapatos, el silencio o el sentido de «We will see». Para descifrarlo: 1) ¿qué pasó?, 2) ¿qué esperaba cada uno?, 3) ¿cuál es la mejor reacción? Suele ser preguntar con tacto y explicar tu costumbre, sin acusar. Frases útiles: «I assumed that…», «In my country it is usual to…», «I did not realise that…».

patron.texto: I assumed that + lo que creía, but + lo que ocurre:

formula.texto: but they usually eat at six.
formula.nota: realidad: lo que hace la otra familia

filas.texto: Is it the custom to take them off?

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am embarrassing because I arrived late.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I am embarrassed because I arrived late.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con -ed se describe cómo se siente la persona (embarrassed); -ing describe lo que causa la situación.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: In my country is usual to eat late.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: In my country it is usual to eat late.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En inglés el sujeto it es obligatorio: it is usual to…

situacion.contexto: Sara le explica a Carlos por qué la estudiante de intercambio se sintió incómoda en la cena.

dialogo.texto: Why did Marta look embarrassed at dinner?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Por qué Marta parecía avergonzada en la cena?

dialogo.texto: She assumed that we eat late, so she arrived at eight. We had finished at seven.
dialogo.traduccion: Supuso que cenamos tarde, así que llegó a las ocho. Habíamos terminado a las siete.

dialogo.texto: So it was a misunderstanding, not bad manners.
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces fue un malentendido, no mala educación.

dialogo.texto: Yes. Next time I will tell her our custom and ask about hers.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. La próxima vez le contaré nuestra costumbre y le preguntaré por la suya.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿por qué se sintió incómoda Marta?

opciones.es: Supuso que se cenaba tarde y llegó cuando ya habían terminado.
Llegó demasiado pronto y nadie la saludó.
No le gustó la comida y lo dijo en voz alta.

item.feedback: Sara explica que Marta supuso que cenaban tarde y llegó a las ocho, cuando ya habían terminado.

guiada.consigna: Lee el relato: ¿cuál fue el supuesto que hizo Mia sobre la cena?
guiada.texto: Mia, an exchange student, arrived at her host family's house at eight, wearing her best dress, for a dinner that she assumed would start late. The family had already finished, because they always eat at six. Mia went red and apologised three times.
opciones: That dinner would be late, as at home.
That her host family wanted her to leave early.
That her dress was too formal for an ordinary family dinner.
guiada.feedback: Mia cree que se cena tarde, como en su país: ese supuesto oculto explica que llegue a las ocho cuando ya han terminado.
guiada.pista: Piensa en lo que ella esperaba antes de llegar.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Da a los demás el beneficio de la duda.»
guiada.texto: Before you decide that the family was rude, give them the benefit of the ___. They may simply have assumed that you knew their custom.
guiada.feedback: Give the benefit of the doubt es la expresión fija para suponer buena intención hasta tener pruebas contrarias.

guiada.consigna: Relaciona cada expresión con su significado.
guiada.feedback: Son cuatro piezas de cualquier relato de malentendidos: el problema, la reacción, el contexto y la impresión que se da.
guiada.pista: Piensa en un relato: problema, reacción, lugar e impresión.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué suponía la estudiante que iba a ocurrir en la casa de acogida?
practica.audio: An exchange student from Japan told us that in her country it is polite to refuse a second helping once or twice. In her host family's home, she refused twice and went to bed hungry, because nobody offered a third time. The next morning, her host mother explained that here a refusal is taken at face value. They laughed about it, and since then the family has learned to insist a little, while the student has learned to say yes.
opciones: That a first refusal is polite and will be followed by an offer.
That leaving food on the plate would offend the host mother.
That a student should never accept a second helping.
That a host should decide how much a guest eats.
practica.feedback: Ella suponía que rechazar es educado y que la oferta se repetiría; la familia tomó el rechazo literalmente. Dos supuestos distintos, no mala educación.

practica.consigna: Lee el caso: ¿por qué se sintió avergonzada Sara?
practica.texto: When Sara thanked her host by saying that she would not eat anything else, he took her at her word and cleared the plates. Sara, who had meant that she was almost full, felt embarrassed. Nobody was rude; both had simply assumed that the other used words in the same way.
opciones: Her polite phrase was understood literally.
Her host had not offered her any food.
She had eaten more than the family expected.
Her host thought that she was being rude.
practica.feedback: Sara solo quería decir que estaba casi llena y el anfitrión lo entendió al pie de la letra: hubo dos supuestos, no mala educación.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Nadie quiso hacer daño, pero suponían cosas distintas.»
practica.respuesta: Nobody meant any harm, but they assumed different things
practica.feedback: Nobody meant any harm separa la intención del resultado; but introduce el contraste con assumed different things.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el relato: ¿qué supuesto tenía la familia sobre Marta?
evaluacion.audio: Last spring, Marta, an exchange student from Chile, stayed with a family in Leeds. On her first evening, the father told her to help herself to anything in the kitchen. Marta, who had been raised to wait until food is offered, thanked him and stayed hungry until breakfast. The family, in turn, noticed that she never opened the fridge and assumed that she was unhappy or shy. Only after a week did the mother say, over tea, that in their house guests are expected to serve themselves, and that asking is not needed. Marta burst out laughing, and so did everyone else. From then on, the fridge became the centre of their conversations.
opciones: That she was unhappy or shy, since she never opened the fridge.
That she disliked the food that the family usually cooked for guests.
That she expected the mother to serve her every meal.
That she was used to eating alone in her own room.
evaluacion.feedback: Cada lado suponía algo distinto: Marta esperaba que le ofrecieran comida; la familia creyó que era tímida o infeliz por no abrir la nevera.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué reacción le conviene más a Tom la próxima vez, según el caso?
evaluacion.texto: Tom's Japanese colleague smiled slightly and said that Tom's proposal was very interesting, then changed the subject. Tom left the meeting pleased and told his manager that the idea had been approved. A week later he learned that the colleague had meant that the proposal could not go ahead. The colleague felt that a direct refusal would have embarrassed them both.
opciones: Ask what the next step is before reporting an approval.
Tell his manager that the colleague had been rude to him during the meeting.
Stop presenting proposals to colleagues from other countries.
Insist until the colleague finally answers yes or no in plain words.
evaluacion.feedback: Preguntar con tacto por el siguiente paso evita suponer un sí; acusar, rendirse o forzar una respuesta directa ignora que el colega quiso evitar la vergüenza.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Puede dar la impresión de ser tímido.»
evaluacion.texto: A guest who never speaks during dinner may come ___ as shy, although in his family silence is a sign of respect.
evaluacion.feedback: Come across as describe la impresión que causa alguien, que puede no coincidir con su intención real.

evaluacion.consigna: Relaciona cada situación con el supuesto que la explica.
pares: A guest arrives at eight for a dinner planned for six
supuesto sobre la hora de la cena
A student keeps her shoes on where everybody takes them off
supuesto sobre los zapatos dentro de casa
A manager says “We will see” and the visitor hears a yes
supuesto sobre el sentido de una frase cortés
A host stays silent at dinner and the student thinks he is angry
supuesto sobre el significado del silencio
evaluacion.feedback: En cada caso nadie fue maleducado: dos personas aplicaron reglas distintas a la misma situación.

repaso.consigna: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe la columna sobre los malentendidos?
repaso.texto: We like to think that travel opens the mind, yet most misunderstandings come from a simple failure to think. We assume that our habits are the normal setting everywhere, and when a host acts differently, we explain it as bad manners. Curiosity, not patience, is the better response: ask first, judge later.
opciones: Asking questions beats simply being patient.
Travel makes people more open in almost every case.
Bad manners are the main cause of trouble between countries.
Guests should wait patiently and let hosts explain their customs.
repaso.feedback: Considera que la paciencia no basta y propone preguntar antes de juzgar; el origen del problema es suponer que nuestras costumbres son universales.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Concede a tu anfitrión el beneficio de la duda.»
repaso.respuesta: Give your host the benefit of the doubt
repaso.feedback: Give + persona + the benefit of the doubt: el anfitrión va antes de la expresión fija.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué quiere aclarar Sara a Marta?
repaso.audio: Hello Marta, it is Sara. I am sorry about last night. When I told you that we would see about Sunday, I did not mean yes. In my family that is a polite no. I should have said so clearly, and I hope that you did not take offence.
opciones: That “we will see” was a refusal, not a promise.
That Sunday is the best day for a family dinner.
That Marta should ask before accepting an invitation.
That her family always says no to every invitation.
repaso.feedback: Sara explica que su «we would see» era un no cortés, reconoce que debió decirlo con claridad y pide que no se haya ofendido.

classes.objetivo: Explicar una costumbre familiar a un visitante con generalizaciones matizadas, un ejemplo concreto y una comparación respetuosa.

ensenanza.en: Our Sunday lunch is an old custom and a long-standing tradition, and relatives tend to arrive around noon.
ensenanza.es: Nuestro almuerzo del domingo es una vieja costumbre y una tradición de larga data, y los parientes suelen llegar hacia el mediodía.
ensenanza.nota: Se presenta la costumbre y se matiza con tend to.

ensenanza.en: By and large, a visitor is welcome at our table without an invitation, and a warm welcome is part of the custom.
ensenanza.es: En general, un visitante es bienvenido en nuestra mesa sin invitación, y una cálida bienvenida forma parte de la costumbre.
ensenanza.nota: Generalización matizada: «en general», no «siempre».

ensenanza.en: For example, we all share one big dish from the centre of the table as a gesture of hospitality.
ensenanza.es: Por ejemplo, todos compartimos un plato grande del centro de la mesa como gesto de hospitalidad.
ensenanza.nota: For example introduce un ejemplo concreto que ilustra la costumbre.

ensenanza.en: Some cultures serve separate plates, whereas in mine the shared dish may strike a visitor as unusual at first.
ensenanza.es: Algunas culturas sirven platos separados, mientras que en la mía el plato compartido puede parecerle inusual a un visitante al principio.
ensenanza.nota: Whereas contrasta dos costumbres sin juzgar ninguna.

ensenanza.en: A custom that is second nature to us is easy to overlook, but a visitor notices it at once.
ensenanza.es: Una costumbre que para nosotros es algo natural es fácil de pasar por alto, pero un visitante la nota de inmediato.
ensenanza.nota: Lo automático para unos es lo llamativo para otros.

ensenanza.en: In many households it is customary to bring a small gift, and the host will share the best seat with a guest.
ensenanza.es: En muchas casas es costumbre llevar un pequeño regalo, y el anfitrión comparte el mejor asiento con el invitado.
ensenanza.nota: It is customary to + verbo base: «es costumbre» sin culpar a nadie.

explicacion.texto: Para explicar una costumbre a alguien de fuera: 1) presenta qué es y cuándo ocurre; 2) generaliza con cuidado (tend to, by and large: no todos, no siempre); 3) da un ejemplo concreto (for example); 4) compara sin juzgar con whereas, in some countries… o neither way is better. Evita «we are right / you are strange». Si algo puede sorprender, avísalo: «It may seem unusual at first». En español a veces decimos «eso es raro»; en inglés suena mejor different.

formula.texto: and relatives tend to arrive at noon.
For example, we all share one dish,
whereas in some countries people eat separately.

filas.texto: For example, we share one dish.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: We have this custom since many years.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: We have had this custom for many years.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con una duración se usa for y el present perfect: have had… for many years; since se reserva para un punto de partida.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The visitors must to take off their shoes.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The visitors must take off their shoes.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Must va seguido del verbo base, sin to; la forma con to es have to (have to take off).

situacion.contexto: Ana explica a Tom, que viene de otro país, cómo es el almuerzo del domingo en su casa.

dialogo.texto: Is it true that everyone shares the same dish at your Sunday lunch?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Es verdad que todos comparten el mismo plato en el almuerzo del domingo de tu familia?

dialogo.texto: By and large, yes. We tend to put one big dish in the middle.
dialogo.traduccion: En general, sí. Solemos poner un plato grande en el centro.

dialogo.texto: In my country we each have our own plate.
dialogo.traduccion: En mi país cada uno tiene su propio plato.

dialogo.texto: Neither way is better. Whereas you eat separately, we like to share.
dialogo.traduccion: Ninguna forma es mejor. Mientras que en tu país cada uno come por separado, a nosotros nos gusta compartir.

opciones.es: Sin decir que una sea mejor: señala la diferencia.
Dice que su costumbre es mejor que la de Tom.
Dice que la costumbre de Tom es extraña.

item.feedback: Ana dice «Neither way is better» y usa whereas para contrastar: describe la diferencia sin juzgar.

guiada.consigna: ¿Cómo debería corregir la estudiante esta explicación de su costumbre?
guiada.texto: A student is describing the dinner time in her family: “In my country everybody eats dinner at ten, which is much better than the silly habit of eating at six.” Her teacher asks for a version that a visitor could hear without feeling hurt.
opciones: In my country families tend to eat at ten, whereas in yours it is earlier.
In my country we eat at ten, which is obviously the only correct time for dinner.
In my country eating at six is strange, so you should really change your habit.
In my country nobody ever eats at six, unlike all other countries.
guiada.feedback: Tend to matiza la generalización y whereas contrasta sin juzgar; las demás versiones elogian la propia costumbre o rechazan la ajena.
guiada.pista: Busca la versión que describe la diferencia sin decir cuál es mejor.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «El plato compartido puede parecerle inusual a un visitante.»
guiada.texto: In my house everybody shares one big dish, and this may ___ a visitor as unusual at first, although by the end of the evening it seems natural.
guiada.feedback: Strike someone as + adjetivo describe la impresión que algo causa a una persona, sin juzgar lo que es.
guiada.pista: Verbo que significa «golpear», pero aquí describe una impresión.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Ninguna forma es mejor porque cada costumbre tiene sentido en casa.»
guiada.respuesta: Neither way is better because each custom makes sense at home
guiada.feedback: Neither way is better + because + causa: la comparación respetuosa explica por qué no hay un ganador.
guiada.pista: Empieza con neither way y termina con at home.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué actitud tiene quien narra hacia la costumbre de su abuela?
practica.audio: My grandmother has a custom that surprises every visitor: before anyone eats, she puts a little food on a small plate by the window. She says it is a gesture of hospitality for anyone who might be passing. Whereas my cousins find it odd, I find it moving, because it reminds me that a welcome does not end at the front door.
opciones: It moves the narrator, although the cousins consider it odd.
It moves the narrator, and the cousins feel exactly the same.
It seems strange to the narrator, as it does to the cousins.
It worries the narrator whenever a visitor asks about it.
practica.feedback: Contrasta con whereas: sus primos la consideran rara, pero a quien narra le emociona porque recuerda que la bienvenida no termina en la puerta.

practica.consigna: Lee la situación: ¿qué frase compara dos costumbres con respeto?
practica.texto: A student is explaining to an exchange student how her family celebrates birthdays. She wants to describe the difference without sounding better than anybody else, and she is looking for the best sentence to use.
opciones: In my family we tend to sing first, whereas in many countries people cut the cake first.
In my family we tend to sing first, which is obviously the correct way.
In other countries people tend to cut the cake first, whereas we do it the right way.
Everybody in my family always sings first, unlike all other countries.
practica.feedback: Tend to y whereas describen la diferencia sin juicio; las otras opciones, aunque usen las mismas estructuras, declaran una costumbre correcta o universal.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «En general, los visitantes son bienvenidos a nuestra mesa.»
practica.respuesta: By and large, visitors are welcome at our table
practica.feedback: By and large abre la frase y matiza; visitors are welcome at our table es la generalización.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué quiere transmitir quien habla al describir las costumbres de su casa?
evaluacion.audio: When visitors first come to my house, they usually notice three things: the shoes by the door, the very long goodbye and the fact that my mother will not let anyone help in the kitchen. At first glance these habits may strike them as strange. By and large, however, they leave understanding that each one is a gesture of welcome: the shoes keep the floor clean for the children, the long goodbye shows that nobody is in a hurry, and the empty kitchen is my mother's way of saying that a guest is a guest. Whereas in my friend's home everybody cooks together, in ours the cook is the host. Neither way is better; both are ways of saying: you matter.
opciones: That habits which look odd are gestures of welcome with their own logic.
That visitors should copy her customs as soon as they arrive.
That her mother's kitchen rules are stricter than other families' rules.
That cooking together is a better custom than cooking alone.
evaluacion.feedback: Cada hábito que sorprende resulta ser un gesto de bienvenida con su lógica; la comparación final, «neither way is better», evita juzgar.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué corrección propone quien revisa el borrador?
evaluacion.texto: Your paragraph about Sunday lunch is warm and vivid, and the example of the shared dish works well. However, the sentence “In other countries people are cold at meals” is an unfair generalisation, and it undermines the respectful tone of the rest. A better comparison would describe what people do, not what they are.
opciones: Replace the judgement by a description of behaviour.
Delete the shared dish example because it is too personal.
Remove every comparison with other countries from the paragraph.
Soften “cold” to “a bit cold” so that the generalisation sounds fairer.
evaluacion.feedback: Elogia el ejemplo y el tono cálido, pero el juicio «cold» sobre otras personas debe sustituirse por lo que hacen: describir conductas, no rasgos.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «En algunas casas es costumbre quitarse los zapatos al entrar.»
evaluacion.texto: Guests do not always know the rules of a new house, but in some homes it is ___ to take off your shoes at the door, and a polite visitor does it without being asked.
evaluacion.feedback: It is customary to + verbo base es la fórmula de registro más formal para «es costumbre».

evaluacion.consigna: Explica una costumbre de tu familia a un visitante (180–240 palabras).
evaluacion.texto: Explica a un visitante extranjero una costumbre de tu familia (la cena del viernes, el almuerzo del domingo…). Escribe en inglés con dos generalizaciones matizadas (by and large, tend to…), un ejemplo concreto y una comparación respetuosa con otra costumbre.
evaluacion.respuesta: In my family, Friday dinner is a long-standing tradition. By and large, everybody is home by seven, and the children tend to choose the menu. For example, last week my little brother asked for rice and chicken, and we all agreed. A visitor is always welcome, and guests usually bring a dessert or a small gift. It is customary to share one big dish from the centre of the table, which may strike a visitor as unusual at first. In many countries each person has a separate plate, whereas in mine we pass the food around and talk while we eat. Neither way is better; each custom makes sense at home. Please do not worry if you are unsure what to do: my mother will show you, and she will give you a warm welcome. I hope that you can join us one Friday.
aceptadas: Every Sunday my family has lunch at my grandmother's house, a custom that is older than I am. As a rule, everybody arrives around noon, and the younger cousins tend to arrive last. For instance, last month my uncle brought a cake that he had baked himself, and we all laughed because it was still warm. Visitors are welcome too, and they usually sit next to my grandmother. In some countries people eat quickly and leave, whereas in mine the table is a place to stay and talk for hours. Neither way is wrong; each custom simply suits its own home. It may seem unusual at first, but guests quickly feel at ease. I would love to see you there one Sunday.
evaluacion.feedback: Un texto completo presenta la costumbre, matiza dos generalizaciones, da un ejemplo concreto y compara con respeto, sin juzgar.

repaso.consigna: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe sobre explicar una costumbre a un extraño?
repaso.texto: Some people claim that explaining a custom to a stranger makes it sound less natural, as if we were showing our family in a museum. I see it differently. A custom that we cannot explain is one that we have stopped noticing, and describing it kindly is a way of keeping it alive and of inviting the stranger in.
opciones: Explaining a custom values it and welcomes strangers.
Explaining a custom makes it sound less natural, so it is best avoided.
Only customs that are very old deserve an explanation.
Strangers should learn the customs without asking questions.
repaso.feedback: Rebate la idea del museo: explicar con cariño mantiene viva la costumbre y abre la puerta al extraño.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Mientras que nosotros compartimos un plato, ellos usan platos separados.»
repaso.respuesta: Whereas we share one dish, they use separate plates
aceptadas: They use separate plates, whereas we share one dish
repaso.feedback: Whereas une dos hechos contrastados; puede abrir la frase o ir en medio, separado por coma.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué actitud muestra Ana al explicar la costumbre?
repaso.audio: Hi Tom, it is Ana. About Saturday: at our house we tend to take off our shoes at the door, so bring some warm socks. It is not a rule, just a habit, and my mother will lend you some if you forget. She would be very happy if you tried her dessert, which is an old family recipe.
opciones: Relaxed and welcoming: she explains a habit, not a demand.
Formal: she lists conditions that Tom must accept to be welcome.
Nervous: she worries that Tom will dislike her family's customs.
Defensive: she justifies her family's habits before Tom can judge them.
repaso.feedback: Dice «not a rule, just a habit» y ofrece una solución si olvida algo: explica una costumbre con calidez y sin imponerla.

classes.objetivo: Recibir a un invitado extranjero: explicar dos costumbres con matices, aclarar un malentendido con tacto y responder a una pregunta incómoda.

vocabulario.es: no quise decir, no era mi intención

ensenanza.en: Please feel at home: a guest who is afraid to open the fridge will never relax, however kind the welcome.
ensenanza.es: Siéntete como en casa: un invitado que tiene miedo de abrir la nevera nunca se relajará, por amable que sea la bienvenida.
ensenanza.nota: Feel at home es una bienvenida cálida que da permiso al invitado.

ensenanza.en: If a misunderstanding has spoiled the evening, apologise briefly and tactfully, without blaming the guest.
ensenanza.es: Si un malentendido ha estropeado la velada, discúlpate con brevedad y con tacto, sin culpar al invitado.
ensenanza.nota: Apologise reconoce un fallo sin dramatizar; se dice apologise for…

ensenanza.en: Let me clarify: we did not mean to ignore you when we started eating, because in our house nobody waits after seven.
ensenanza.es: Déjame aclarar: no queríamos ignorarte cuando empezamos a comer, porque en nuestra casa nadie espera después de las siete.
ensenanza.nota: Clarify + did not mean: aclara la intención sin culpar a nadie.

ensenanza.en: When the guest asks an awkward question, say “Good question” and tread carefully: answer honestly, but without absolute words.
ensenanza.es: Cuando el invitado hace una pregunta incómoda, di «Buena pregunta» y ve con cuidado: responde con honestidad, pero sin palabras absolutas.
ensenanza.nota: Reconocer lo delicado y responder sin «siempre» ni «nunca» evita una discusión.

ensenanza.en: To clear the air after a clash, set the record straight about your custom and invite the guest to ask anything.
ensenanza.es: Para despejar el ambiente tras un choque, aclara las cosas sobre tu costumbre e invita al invitado a preguntar lo que quiera.
ensenanza.nota: Clear the air y set the record straight buscan reparar, no ganar.

ensenanza.en: “No offence” is a softener for criticism, so use it sparingly, and never after an awkward remark that has already hurt someone.
ensenanza.es: «Sin ofender» suaviza una crítica, así que úsalo con moderación y nunca tras un comentario incómodo que ya ha herido a alguien.
ensenanza.nota: No offence no borra una ofensa: solo suaviza lo que aún no se ha dicho.

explicacion.titulo: Recibir a un invitado sin choques
explicacion.texto: Recibir a un invitado extranjero combina tres habilidades. Primero, da la bienvenida y explica tus costumbres con matices (We tend to…, By and large…). Segundo, si hay un malentendido, aclara sin culpar: Let me clarify…, We did not mean to…, I apologise for… Tercero, ante una pregunta incómoda, reconócela con calidez (Good question!), responde con honestidad amable y evita «siempre» y «nunca». El objetivo no es tener razón, sino que el invitado se sienta a gusto (feel at home).

formula.texto: We tend to take off our shoes,
we did not mean to be rude.

filas.texto: We tend to eat at six.
Let me clarify: we did not mean to be rude.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I apologise you for the confusion.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Apologise va seguido de for + motivo; si quieres nombrar a la persona, se añade to: I apologise to you for…

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Please, you feel like in your house.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: «Sentirse como en casa» se dice feel at home; no se traduce palabra por palabra.

situacion.contexto: Carlos, un invitado extranjero, y Sara, su anfitriona, hablan durante la cena.

dialogo.texto: Why is nobody eating? The food is on the table.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Por qué no come nadie? La comida está en la mesa.

dialogo.texto: Let me clarify: in my family we wait until everybody sits down. I should have told you.
dialogo.traduccion: Déjame aclarar: en mi familia esperamos a que todos se sienten. Debería habértelo dicho.

dialogo.texto: No problem. Can I ask something? Do families here never talk at dinner?
dialogo.traduccion: Sin problema. ¿Puedo preguntar algo? ¿Las familias de aquí nunca hablan en la cena?

dialogo.texto: Good question! By and large, we talk a lot, but some families tend to be quiet.
dialogo.traduccion: ¡Buena pregunta! En general hablamos mucho, pero algunas familias suelen ser calladas.

item.consigna: ¿Cómo responde Sara a la pregunta de Carlos?

opciones.es: Con amabilidad y matices, sin decir «siempre» ni «nunca».
Diciendo que todas las familias hablan siempre.
Negándose a contestar porque la pregunta es incómoda.

item.feedback: Sara reconoce la pregunta con «Good question!» y responde con by and large y tend to, sin absolutos.

guiada.consigna: Lee el intercambio: ¿por qué es diplomática la respuesta de Sara?
guiada.texto: Carlos, a guest from abroad, asks his hosts why nobody talks during dinner. Sara smiles and answers, “Good question! By and large we talk a lot, but tonight we were all very tired.” Carlos laughs, and the silence disappears.
opciones: It welcomes the question and avoids absolute words.
It avoids the question by changing the subject quickly.
It admits that the family is unfriendly to every guest.
guiada.feedback: Sara reconoce la pregunta con «Good question!» y responde con by and large y una razón concreta, sin absolutos ni evasivas.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en cómo empieza su respuesta y en las palabras que evita.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Ana preparó té para despejar el ambiente.»
guiada.texto: After the argument at dinner, nobody wanted to speak first, so Ana made tea to clear the ___ between them and offer a fresh start.
guiada.feedback: Clear the air es la expresión fija para disipar la tensión tras una discusión o un malentendido.

guiada.consigna: Relaciona cada expresión del anfitrión con su función.
guiada.feedback: Cada expresión cumple un papel distinto al recibir a un invitado: aclarar, suavizar, acoger y responder con tacto.
guiada.pista: Piensa en el orden de una visita: bienvenida, malentendido, pregunta.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué hizo especialmente bien el padre al contestar a la invitada?
practica.audio: Our guest from Canada arrived on Friday and asked why we never eat before eight. My father said, “Good question. Most families here tend to eat late, but it is only a habit, and we can eat earlier if you prefer.” The guest looked relieved. She said later that nobody had ever answered her so kindly, and that she felt at home by the end of the evening.
opciones: He explained the habit and offered to adapt it if the guest preferred.
He explained the habit but insisted that the guest must follow it.
He offered to change the habit without explaining why it exists.
He apologised for the habit and promised to abandon it for good.
practica.feedback: Reconoce la pregunta, describe el hábito con «tend to» y se ofrece a adaptarlo: así la invitada se siente en casa.

practica.consigna: Lee el mensaje: ¿qué busca quien lo escribe?
practica.texto: I apologise for what happened at dinner. We did not mean to leave you out; in our house the cook eats last and the guests start first, so we assumed that you would begin. Please tell me if anything else surprises you.
opciones: To clear the air by explaining the custom kindly.
To excuse the family by proving that the guest was in the wrong.
To ask the guest to follow the customs of the house from now on.
To cancel the invitation politely without saying so.
practica.feedback: Se disculpa, explica la costumbre (la cocinera come la última) y deja la puerta abierta a más preguntas, sin culpar al invitado.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Por favor, siéntete como en casa y pregúntame lo que quieras.»
practica.respuesta: Please feel at home and ask me anything
practica.feedback: Feel at home es una expresión fija; ask me anything invita al invitado a preguntar sin reservas.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el relato: ¿cómo arregla la familia la situación con Jamal?
evaluacion.audio: When Jamal, an exchange student from Kenya, came to stay with us, my mother gave him a list of house rules, which was the first mistake. The second was my father's joke that only tourists ask for a second blanket. Jamal smiled politely, but the next morning he looked tired. My mother, who reads faces well, took me aside and suggested that we apologise for the joke, clarify that the list was not an order, and offer a blanket without comment. At breakfast my father said, with a smile, that he had been a bad host and a worse performer. Jamal laughed, accepted the blanket, and asked whether the house rules included the recipe for my mother's bread.
opciones: By saying sorry for the joke, making clear the list was no order and giving him a blanket.
By asking Jamal to explain why he had not slept well that night.
By removing the house rules and inviting him to write his own list.
By telling Jamal politely that a second blanket was not really needed.
evaluacion.feedback: La familia se disculpa por la broma, aclara que la lista no era una orden y ofrece la manta sin comentarios: reparar sin culpar.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué busca quien escribe al responder así a la pregunta incómoda de Hana?
evaluacion.texto: Dear Hana, you asked whether all the families in our town are as quiet as mine. It is a good question, and I should say first that I can only speak for the families I know. Many of them tend to be reserved at dinner, but others are noisy, particularly on Sundays. Please do not take our quiet as a sign that we are cold; it is simply how we were brought up.
opciones: To reply frankly to a difficult question, limited to what the writer knows.
To avoid the question by praising the families the writer knows.
To prove that every family in the town is quieter than Hana's.
To apologise because the writer's family is so different from Hana's.
evaluacion.feedback: Acota («only speak for the families I know»), matiza con «many» y «tend to» y explica sin disculparse: una respuesta sincera y sin absolutos.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Déjame aclarar lo que pasó anoche.»
evaluacion.texto: I did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you, so let me set the record ___ about what happened last night.
evaluacion.feedback: Set the record straight es la expresión fija para corregir una impresión equivocada.

evaluacion.consigna: Da la bienvenida a tu invitado, aclara y responde con tacto (200–260 palabras).
evaluacion.texto: Tu invitado Carlos llega de otro país. Escribe en inglés: da la bienvenida, explica dos costumbres con matices (tend to, by and large), aclara un malentendido (por ejemplo, que empezaron a comer sin él) con Let me clarify… y responde con tacto a su pregunta: «Why do you not talk more at dinner?».
evaluacion.respuesta: Welcome, Carlos, and please feel at home! In my family we tend to eat dinner at six, and by and large everybody helps to set the table. Let me clarify something about last night: we did not mean to be rude when we started eating without you. I apologise, because I should have explained that we usually do not wait after seven. You asked a good question: why do we not talk more at dinner? It is a fair thing to wonder, and I will try to answer tactfully. Some families are quieter, and ours likes to enjoy the food first, whereas in your country people seem to talk more. Neither way is better, and it is only a habit; nobody is upset. Tomorrow we will talk as much as you like, and I will show you the city. No offence if we are quiet again on Sunday: my grandmother cooks, and we tend to listen to her stories.
aceptadas: Hello, Hana, make yourself at home! As a rule, my family has breakfast together at eight, and we tend to be quiet because we are still sleepy. Let me explain something about this morning: we did not mean to ignore you when we stayed silent. I am sorry, because I should have told you about our custom. That is a fair question: why is nobody talking at the table? In some houses people talk a lot at breakfast, whereas in ours we like silence and coffee first. It is only a habit, and nobody is upset. At lunch we will talk as much as you like, and I promise to ask you about your country and your family. I hope that you will feel at ease with us very soon.
evaluacion.feedback: El texto da la bienvenida, explica costumbres con matices, aclara el malentendido sin culpar y responde con tacto a la pregunta.

evidencias: let me set the record straight

repaso.consigna: ¿Cuál es la actitud de quien escribe ante los invitados de otros países?
repaso.texto: Hosting a foreigner taught me that politeness has no universal grammar. Some guests want to be left alone; others think that being left alone means being ignored. I used to worry that every choice would offend someone. Now I explain my habits openly and ask about theirs, which costs nothing and avoids most of the damage.
opciones: Open explanation and questions are better than guessing what offends.
Guests should accept every habit of the host without asking.
It is wiser to avoid inviting people from other countries.
Hosts should leave every guest alone to avoid any problem.
repaso.feedback: Ya no adivina qué ofende: explica sus hábitos y pregunta por los del invitado, una estrategia sin coste que evita casi todo el daño.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Déjame aclarar lo que no quisimos decir.»
repaso.respuesta: Let me clarify what we did not mean to say
repaso.feedback: Let me clarify + what + oración: aclara la intención sin culpar a nadie.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el mensaje del invitado: ¿qué quiere transmitir?
repaso.audio: Thank you for the lovely evening. Your question about my country was not awkward at all, although I am afraid my answer was too long. Please tell me if I talk too much. Back home we say that a guest who is shy at the start is a guest who will be very happy in the end.
opciones: That the guest enjoyed the evening and feels comfortable with the family.
That the guest was offended by the question about the guest's country.
That the guest regrets having accepted the invitation.
That the guest thinks the family talks too much at dinner.
repaso.feedback: Agradece la velada, resta importancia a su respuesta larga y cierra con un proverbio que muestra que se siente a gusto.

notes: Claves verificadas; c16 practica 1 tenía dos opciones defendibles (pista y ausencia de fecha) y c19 practica 0 tenía un dato falso en la clave (primos que se ríen): corregidos.
Distractores de c16-c20 reescritos como casi-aciertos; c19 eval completar ya no repite la frase de la enseñanza; c16 eval completar sin solapamiento.
c17 escribir pasa a rúbrica flexible (tend to/by and large + referencia + contenido); rúbricas c19/c20 sin palabras sueltas; error de léxico 'foreigners' en c19 eliminado.
